newsitem.title: INDIA: Rich nations must fulfil environment vows - India.
newsitem.headline: Rich nations must fulfil environment vows - India.

text.p: India will call on developed countries at an environment meeting next week to fulfil commitments they made at the Earth Summit five years ago, Environment Minister Saifuddin Soz said on Wednesday.
He said India also felt it was premature to begin talks on a legal international convention on forests, on which United Nations members are considering negotiations.

More than 65 government leaders are due to meet in New York at the second Earth Summit from June 23-27 to review progress in environmental protection five years after the landmark Rio de Janeiro meeting.
"Industrialised countries are taking a stand where they are refusing to take responsibility for their commitments and are diluting them," Soz told a news conference.
"They are also trying to impose conditions on developing countries like us. This is unacceptable and cannot be allowed," he said without elaborating.
Countries such as Canada, Malaysia and Russia favour a legal convention on forests, which the United States opposes. Like Brazil, India wants to consider the question later.
"We feel that there is still need for further discussion to arrive at a clear consensus," Soz said. "We will accept only a convention that keeps our sovereignty intact."

Referring to a proposed international convention on chemicals, the minister said: "We have taken the stand that there is a need first to look at the availability of substitutes in the area of fertilisers as well as carry out risk assessment studies."
India also planned to be the first country in the world to introduce a law on protecting its biodiversity by August, Soz said.
